4. Baseline gate is green: `cargo test --locked -p moe-windows-job-core` => 7 passed, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.note:
THE REOPEN FIX LANDS HERE. Commit 55dea5d, one file, +27/-9, explicit pathspec.

QA's finding verified before touching anything, by reading the file rather than trusting the report. `OwnedAttributeList::as_ptr(&self)` derives from `Vec::as_ptr`, whose contract forbids writing through it or through any pointer derived from it. That pointer was the DESTINATION of UpdateProcThreadAttribute at both attribute arms, and that call WRITES the attribute into the buffer. Both call sites already held `list: &mut OwnedAttributeList`, so mutable provenance was available and only the shared reborrow was wrong: UB under Stacked and Tree Borrows, and Vec<usize> is Freeze so LLVM may apply readonly/noalias reasoning across the FFI call. Confirmed, not disputed.

FIX: added `OwnedAttributeList::as_mut_ptr(&mut self)` deriving from `self.buffer.as_mut_ptr()` — the same derivation `delete()` already used — and pointed both destinations at it (set_job_list, set_handle_list). SAFETY comments updated to say why the destination is mutable and the value is not.

HELD THE LINE ON WHAT QA SAID NOT TO CHANGE, verified by grep over src/:
- `as_ptr()` survives with exactly ONE caller, system_process.rs:187, storing the list in STARTUPINFOEXW::lpAttributeList for CreateProcessW to READ. Not converted wholesale.
- The VALUE pointers stay const: `ptr::addr_of!(*list.job)` and `list.handles.as_ptr()`. The list only records them; CreateProcessW reads through them and nothing writes. Making them mutable would have been a second defect, not a fix.

Checked deliberately, because if it did, QA's fix would have traded one UB for another.

planningNotes.risks:
1. 2a's suite exercises the real windows-sys calls ZERO times -- everything runs through the scripted double, and tests/real_windows.rs belongs to 2b. So a green 2a proves system_process.rs COMPILES, never that it WORKS. Do not describe the release build as behavioural evidence in the completion report. This is a known and accepted seam, closed by 2b.

2. system_process.rs is the file most likely to breach 250 lines; the attribute-list arm alone needs a two-call size probe, a correctly aligned owned buffer, and a JOB handle whose storage must outlive CreateProcessW. Contingency is pre-authorised in step 7: split the attribute-list arms into src/win32/system_process_attrs.rs. That is a 9th file and still inside the 10-file ceiling. Do not instead compress by deleting SAFETY comments.

3. ATTRIBUTE LIFETIME IS THE REAL FOOTGUN. UpdateProcThreadAttribute stores a POINTER to lpvalue; it does not copy. The job handle passed for JOB_LIST and the handle array passed for HANDLE_LIST must both stay alive and un-moved until CreateProcessW returns. A local temporary or a moved Vec here is a use-after-free that will pass every scripted test in this task, because the double never dereferences anything. Own that storage inside the same struct that owns the attribute list.

4. bInheritHandles must be TRUE for PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST to mean anything, and every handle in the allowlist must itself be inheritable. An allowlist passed with bInheritHandles FALSE silently inherits nothing and the child gets no stdio -- invisible until 2b runs a real process.

5. IsProcessInJob has two failure modes that must NOT collapse: the call failing (BOOL 0 -> NativeOp::IsProcessInJob with GetLastError) versus the call succeeding while reporting false (-> NativeOp::IsProcessInJob with code 0, our refusal). Both must be separately tested; a single test asserting "membership refused" satisfies neither the global rail nor DoD item 4. Same shape for ResumeThread: u32::MAX is a Win32 failure, a successful call returning a prior count other than 1 is our refusal with code 0.

6. The order test must assert the FULL recorded call sequence with assert_eq! on the whole vector, exactly as child 1's successful_creation_calls_create_set_query_in_order does. A test that only asserts resume appears after membership can pass with an entire step missing.

7. Shared working directory: `git status --porcelain` is dirty with many foreign .moe/ files. Commit by explicit pathspec over the 8 owned paths only, and record the repo-wide baseline in step 1 so any foreign red is path-attributable rather than yours.
